The image shows soybean plants at ground level with:
- Green stems remaining green/moist while pods are present
- Some yellowing leaves (one bright yellow leaf visible)
- Brown/dead leaf tissue on some leaves
- Generally the plant appears to have delayed senescence with green stems persisting
- No obvious fungal structures, pustules, or clear necrotic lesions

Key observation: The stems are green and moist-looking while there's mixed maturity across the plant. Some leaves are dying (brown), one is yellow, but the stems remain green. This pattern of green stems persisting while other plant parts show senescence is characteristic of **Green_stem_disorder**.

The plant doesn't show clear signs of fungal disease (no white mold, no rust pustules, no frogeye spots). The main feature is the green, turgid stems with delayed maturity signs.
